knowledge:
- key_parameters: shiftSize=The distance between adjacent intervals (overlap size) in number of SNVs ;; intervalSize=The size of each interval to be analyzed in number of SNVs ;; haplotypes=Logical indicating whether the data is phased haplotypes (TRUE) or unphased genotypes (FALSE) ;; Lt=Threshold for FABIA model loadings (default 0.1) to identify tagSNVs ;; Zt=Threshold for FABIA model factors (default 0.2) to identify individuals belonging to the IBD segment ;; thresCount=P-value threshold for the binomial test to identify local accumulations of tagSNVs (default 1e-5) ;; mintagSNVsFactor=Factor to determine the minimum number of tagSNVs for core individuals (default 3/4) ;; pMAF=Minor allele frequency threshold for tagSNVs
- alternatives: BIMAX and QUBIC are standard biclustering methods, but FABIA is preferred because it can represent homozygous regions (via multiplicative factors) and overlapping IBD segments (via additive factors) in diploid individuals. Standard IBD detection methods are also alternatives but fail on very short segments because they do not utilize rare variants or share information across multiple individuals.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you want to detect very short, old IBD segments shared among multiple individuals in large sequencing datasets, utilizing rare variants from phased/unphased genotypes, minor allele likelihoods, or dosages.
- pitfalls: Sourcing the pipeline can take a long time for large datasets. When plotting, the filename argument must be specified without the ".txt" extension. Phasing errors in the input data can lead to split chromosomes showing up as separate lines in the visualization. Spurious correlations at the borders of IBD segments can cause overestimation of segment length if not pruned.

workflows.name: vcf_pipeline
workflows.intent: Convert a VCF file to sparse matrix format, split it into overlapping intervals, run iterative FABIA, identify duplicates, and analyze/plot the resulting IBD segments.
input: filename.vcf (uncompressed VCF file containing genotype data)
workflows.stages: 1. Convert VCF to sparse matrix format using vcftoFABIA ;; 2. Copy genotype matrix to the active matrix file ;; 3. Split the sparse matrix into overlapping intervals using split_sparse_matrix ;; 4. Run iterative FABIA across intervals using iterateIntervals ;; 5. Identify duplicate IBD segments across overlapping intervals using identifyDuplicates ;; 6. Analyze the non-duplicate IBD segments using analyzeIBDsegments ;; 7. Load and plot specific IBD segments using plot
workflows.code:
shiftSize <- 5000
intervalSize <- 10000
fileName="filename" # without type

library(hapFabia)

vcftoFABIA(fileName=fileName)

file.copy(paste(fileName,"_matG.txt",sep=""),
paste(fileName,"_mat.txt",sep=""))

split_sparse_matrix(fileName=fileName,intervalSize=intervalSize,
shiftSize=shiftSize,annotation=TRUE)

ina <- as.numeric(readLines(paste(fileName,"_mat.txt",sep=""),n=2))
noSNVs <- ina[2]
over <- intervalSize%/%shiftSize
N1 <- noSNVs%/%shiftSize
endRunA <- (N1-over+2)

iterateIntervals(startRun=1,endRun=endRunA,shift=shiftSize,
intervalSize=intervalSize,fileName=fileName,individuals=0,
upperBP=0.05,p=10,iter=40,alpha=0.03,cyc=50,IBDsegmentLength=50,
Lt = 0.1,Zt = 0.2,thresCount=1e-5,mintagSNVsFactor=3/4,
pMAF=0.035,haplotypes=FALSE,cut=0.8,procMinIndivids=0.1,thresPrune=1e-3,
simv="minD",minTagSNVs=6,minIndivid=2,avSNVsDist=100,SNVclusterLength=100)

identifyDuplicates(fileName=fileName,startRun=1,endRun=endRunA,
shift=shiftSize,intervalSize=intervalSize)

anaRes <- analyzeIBDsegments(fileName=fileName,startRun=1,endRun=endRunA,
shift=shiftSize,intervalSize=intervalSize)

posAll <- 50 # (50-1)*5000 = 245000: segment 245000 to 255000
start <- (posAll-1)*shiftSize
end <- start + intervalSize
pRange <- paste("_",format(start,scientific=FALSE),"_",
format(end,scientific=FALSE),sep="")
load(file=paste(fileName,pRange,"_resAnno",".Rda",sep=""))
IBDsegmentList <- resHapFabia$mergedIBDsegmentList

summary(IBDsegmentList)
plot(IBDsegmentList,filename=paste(fileName,pRange,"_mat",sep=""))

IBDsegment <- IBDsegmentList[[1]]
plot(IBDsegment,filename=paste(fileName,pRange,"_mat",sep=""))

workflows.name: direct_sparse_matrix_analysis
workflows.intent: Run the hapFabia analysis directly on pre-existing sparse matrix, annotation, and individual files.
workflows.stages: 1. Run hapFabia directly on the files using hapFabia ;; 2. Summarize the merged IBD segment list ;; 3. Extract and plot a specific IBD segment using plot
workflows.code:
hapRes <- hapFabia(fileName="dataSim1fabia",prefixPath="",
   sparseMatrixPostfix="_mat",
   annotPostfix="_annot.txt",individualsPostfix="_individuals.txt",
   labelsA=NULL,pRange="",individuals=0,lowerBP=0,upperBP=0.15,
   p=10,iter=1,quant=0.01,eps=1e-5,alpha=0.03,cyc=50,non_negative=1,
   write_file=0,norm=0,lap=100.0,IBDsegmentLength=10,Lt = 0.1,
   Zt = 0.2,thresCount=1e-5,mintagSNVsFactor=3/4,pMAF=0.1,
   haplotypes=FALSE,cut=0.8,procMinIndivids=0.1,thresPrune=1e-3,
   simv="minD",minTagSNVs=6,minIndivid=2,avSNVsDist=100,SNVclusterLength=100)

summary(hapRes$mergedIBDsegmentList)

mergedIBDsegmentList <- hapRes$mergedIBDsegmentList # $
IBDsegment <- mergedIBDsegmentList[[1]]

plot(IBDsegment,filename=paste(new_dir,"/dataSim1fabia_mat",sep=""))
